Trump’s Iran “Deal” on a Leash

Iran just yanked Trump’s victory balloon back to earth. One bloody day of Israel–Hezbollah clashes in southern Lebanon, and Tehran simply doesn’t show up in Switzerland for the “permanent peace” talks on war and nukes. No delegation, no new date, JD Vance stays home, and the grand 60‑day roadmap already looks like a countdown to nowhere.

Washington recites lines about free international waterways; operators look at the Persian Gulf Strait Authority and decide whose mood actually moves oil.

Trump screams on Truth Social that Iran is “FINISHED” and “gets no money, not ten cents,” days after signing a memo that unlocks sanctions relief, frozen assets and at least $300 billion in reconstruction commitments because the US and its partners cannot afford another historic energy crunch. 

Tehran calls the US directly responsible for Israel’s Lebanon escalation and openly links its presence at the table to a ceasefire there. That’s not desperation. That’s leverage.

Everyone involved knows 60 days is a joke for a real nuclear agreement — the last one took about two years, and Trump is busy denouncing the deal he already killed once. 

What this delay really exposes is simple: the superpower can still bomb and declare victory; it just can’t control tempo, theater or fallout.

 Iran turned “permanent peace talks” into a variable and the global economy into collateral — and Trump’s big win into a hostage to the next exchange of rockets over southern Lebanon.

🔔 Ripple targets $1B revenue run rate without counting XRP holdings 

❗️ According to posts shared by CoinMarketCap and crypto-focused accounts on X, Ripple expects to end 2026 with a $1 billion revenue run rate. The figure does not include XRP held on Ripple’s balance sheet. That detail matters because Ripple has long faced public debate over the link between its business and XRP. Garlinghouse’s target frames the company as a fintech infrastructure provider that aims to earn money from products, clients, and services, not from token holdings or sales.

🌐 The deal also supports Ripple USD, known as RLUSD. Ripple has promoted the stablecoin for enterprise settlement and collateral use. Recently, crypto news reported that Ripple is also adding RLUSD to new payment tools, including services tied to AI agents and machine payments on the XRP Ledger. Company materials point to custody, treasury management, and liquidity services as core offerings. These products target banks and firms that need faster settlement, account control, and access to digital assets through regulated processes, rather than retail trading.
